CRPF removes jawan from service for posting death threat to Commander on social media
TMC’s Abhishek appears at police station for questioning over social media post

headline: TMC Official Questioned And CRPF Jawan Terminated Over Social Posts
seoTitle: Social Media Posts Lead To Legal And Disciplinary Actions
metaDescription: Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee faces questioning over a social post, while a CRPF jawan is fired for threatening his commander online.
aiSummaryBullets: Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee attended a police station for questioning regarding a May social media post.
The FIR against Banerjee follows allegations that he targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Gujarati community.
A Central Reserve Police Force jawan was terminated from service for issuing a death threat to his commanding officer on social media.
aiContextParagraph: Recent legal and disciplinary actions in India have centered on the use of social media by public figures and government personnel. In the political sphere, Trinamool Congress (TMC) Member of Parliament Abhishek Banerjee was summoned for questioning by police. This follows the registration of an FIR regarding comments made on social media during the assembly election period in May, which allegedly targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Gujarati demographic. Separately, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has dismissed a jawan from duty. The termination occurred after the soldier published a death threat directed at his commanding officer on a social media platform. Following an inquiry led by the Commanding Officer of the involved battalion, the service member was officially removed from his position on November 13, 2026. These events underscore the increasing scrutiny regarding online conduct by prominent figures and security service members.
whyItIsViral: The cluster gained traction due to simultaneous high-profile disciplinary and legal proceedings involving both political figures and national security personnel reported by multiple major outlets.
